item.title: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge: The World's Longest Suspension Span — Guide
item.description: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge leaps nearly four kilometres from the Kobe shore to Awaji Island, crossing one of Japan’s fiercest tidal straits on a central span of 1,991 metres — for many years the longest suspension span in the world. Completed in 1998 after a decade of work, it survived the 1995 Kobe earthquake mid-construction, which shifted its towers and lengthened the span by nearly a metre. From the shore it is simply enormous, best seen lit at night; for those who want more, a maintenance walkway beneath the deck and a guided tour to the top of the 297-metre tower are open to visitors.
